thread.title: UPDATE: As America votes, traders look to profit on the volatility

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: As America votes, traders look to profit on the volatility
text:
By Chris Matthews and Sunny Oh
Longer-horizon managers will delay decisions based on the midterm election's unpredictable effect on the U.S. economy
Tuesday's midterm elections are expected to garner the largest voter turnout in more than 40 years, but voters aren't the only ones paying close attention. Traders interviewed by MarketWatch say that events like Tuesday's elections, which can shift the balance of power in Washington, can create a surge in volatility that makes short-term trading more profitable.
"I'll be staying up and following the returns," said Mike O'Rourke, chief market strategist at Jones Trading.
"Whether there are opportunities out there depends on whether the election results meet expectations," he said, pointing out that the volatility that accompanied the results of the 2016 election created great opportunities for investors who understood the consensus view--that a Trump presidency was bad for markets (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-inauguration-set-to-unleash-cascade-of-stock-market-anxiety-2017-01-19)--was mistaken. The stock market has logged a roughly 28% gain since Trump took office.
Read:Will midterm elections spark a boom in overnight trading? (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/will-midterm-elections-spark-a-boom-in-overnight-trading-2018-11-06)
Vince Reyes, director of trading operations at SEIA, predicts that he'll have a late night this evening followed by an early morning on Wednesday. "We'll see a lot of market action overnight. We're prepared for the unexpected," he said, predicting that if the Republicans can save their House majority, "the market will rip higher 2 or 3%."
Don't miss:The richest man in Florida sees the stock market falling by 15% if Democrats take control of Congress (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-richest-man-in-florida-sees-the-stock-market-falling-by-15-if-democrats-take-control-of-congress-2018-11-06)
He said clients have been buying up FAANG stocks, the tech-concentrated Facebook(FB), Apple(AAPL), Amazon(AMZN), Netflix(NFLX) and Alphabet's Google (GOOGL) shares, which have been beaten up over the past week, in preparation for a surprise result that could redound to the benefit of such growth stocks.
Tom di Galoma, managing director of Treasuries trading at Seaport Global Securities, also plans to be at his terminal into the wee hours of Wednesday, prepared for an election surprise that could "trigger a pretty big move on the rates market," he said. "It pays to be around at your desk and working the markets, and trying to figure out how things will play out. Being in the office is the only way to take advantage of it."
He pointed to the night of the presidential election, when the 10-year Treasury note yield swung in a range of 25 basis points overnight, with yields initially slumping at the prospect of Hillary Clinton's victory then surging as expectations of fiscal stimulus, aka tax cuts, under a Trump presidency gained ground.
On the other hand, if Democrats took over both chambers of Congress it could spark a sharp rally in Treasurys, boosting their prices and driving down yields, in part because of the challenges for a Republican White House in advancing its policies.
Opinion:This is what's happened to stocks after every midterm election since World War II (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/this-is-whats-happened-to-stocks-after-every-midterm-election-since-world-war-ii-2018-11-05)
Money managers with longer-term horizons, however, are avoiding making any decisions based on a midterm result that will have an unpredictable effect on the U.S. economy.
Gibson Smith, chief investment officer for Smith Capital Advisors, said he wasn't going to do much trading on the night, and, at most, invest in some short-maturity bonds to shelter from the potential upsurge in market volatility.
That's a strategy followed by other investors, too. Funds focusing on short-term debt have attracted around $5 billion of inflows in the last four weeks, the largest inflows since Feb. 2016, even as $20 billion gushed out of all other bond funds, according to the Investment Company Institute.
The iShares Treasury 1-3 Year Treasury Bond exchange-traded fund (SHY) has taken in more than $1.1 billion of investor cash in the past five trading sessions, FactSet data shows.
Another factor that makes this election especially important for investors is that corporate executives are also unusually attuned to what's going on in Washington.
According to investment research firm Sentieo, corporate executives are mentioning the midterm elections in corporate documents and regulatory filings in 2018 at nearly twice the rate they did in 2014, and nearly three times as frequently as in 2010.
Consumer discretionary and financial firms are leading this trend. They're paying close attention to Tuesday's results because of their potential impact on trade negotiations with China and other American trade partners.
But even as we learn the results of Tuesday's elections, that doesn't mean we understand the effect they'll have on trade policy, O'Rourke of Jones Trading said.
If the Democrats can win back only the House, they won't have the power to force the president to rescind new tariffs, even if they could agree that would be the right course of action. "The key drivers of the market are peak earnings growth, trade wars and rising interest rates," he said. "I don't see how [the] Democrats taking the House changes those factors."
-Chris Matthews; 1824ET
